arxiv-2001-06768.title: Noise stability of synchronization and optimal network structures
arxiv-2001-06768.creator: Yuriko Katoh, Hiroshi Kori
arxiv-2001-06768.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Yuriko Katoh, Hiroshi Kori. We provide a theoretical framework for quantifying the expected level of synchronization in a network of noisy oscillators. Through linearization around the synchronized state, we derive the following quantities as functions of the eigenvalues and eigenfunctions of the network Laplacian using a standard technique for dealing with multivariate Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes: the magnitude of the fluctuations around a synchronized state and the disturbance coefficients α i \alpha_{i} that represent how strongly node i i disturbs the synchronization.

arxiv-2409-07684.title: Modeling Information Narrative Detection and Evolution on Telegram during the Russia-Ukraine War
arxiv-2409-07684.creator: Patrick Gerard, Svitlana Volkova, Louis Penafiel, Kristina Lerman, Tim Weninger
arxiv-2409-07684.description: Abstract Following the Russian Federation’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, a multitude of information narratives emerged within both pro-Russian and pro-Ukrainian communities online. As the conflict progresses, so too do the information narratives, constantly adapting and influencing local and global community perceptions and attitudes.

arxiv-2501-14986.title: Supercooled Phase Transitions: Why Thermal History of Hidden Sector Matters in Analysis of Pulsar Timing Array Signals
arxiv-2501-14986.creator: Jinzheng Li and Pran Nath
arxiv-2501-14986.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Jinzheng Li and Pran Nath. The detection of a gravitational wave background in the nano-Hertz frequency range from Pulsar Timing Array (PTA) observations offers new insights into evolution of the early universe. In this work we analyze gravitational wave data from PPTA, EPTA, and NANOGrav, as arising from a supercooled first-order phase transition within a hidden sector, characterized by a broken U ​ ( 1 ) X U(1)_{X} gauge symmetry.

arxiv-2503-21971.title: RocketPPA: Code-Level Power, Performance, and Area Prediction via LLM and Mixture of Experts
arxiv-2503-21971.creator: Armin Abdollahi, Mehdi Kamal, and Massoud Pedram
arxiv-2503-21971.description: Abstract This paper presents RocketPPA, a novel ultra-fast power, performance (delay), and area (PPA) estimator operating directly at the code-level abstraction using HDL code as input. The key technical innovation is its LLM-based regression model, which uniquely integrates a large language model (LLM) with a mixture-of-experts (MoE) architecture composed of multilayer perceptrons (MLPs).

arxiv-2509-21832.creator: James A. Rossmanith, Preeti Sar
arxiv-2509-21832.description: Abstract The kinetic Boltzmann equation models gas dynamics over a wide range of spatial and temporal scales. Simplified versions of the full Boltzmann collision operator, such as the classical Bhatnagar-Gross-Krook (BGK) and the closely related Ellipsoidal-Statistical-BGK (ES-BGK) operators, can dramatically decrease the computational costs of numerical solving kinetic equations.

pmc-12596637.description: IntroductionMesonephric-like adenocarcinoma (MLA) is a recently recognized, rare subtype of endometrial carcinoma that can also arise in the ovary. Ovarian MLA is uncommon and often misdiagnosed due to its varied growth patterns and overlap with more common ovarian carcinomas.Presentation of caseWe report a case of ovarian MLA that closely mimicked serous carcinoma clinically and histologically.

pmc-12744320.description: Background: Periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) and superficial wound or skin infection are serious complications following hip arthroplasty for neck of femur (NOF) fractures. pmc-13595422.title: Hyaluronic acid-b-polylactic acid polymersomes facilitate CD44-mediated delivery of doxorubicin to glioblastoma in vitro
pmc-13595422.creator: Apoorvi Chaudhri, Molli Garifo, Pranavi Thatavarthi, Torrick Fletcher, Jessica Larsen
pmc-13595422.description: Glioblastoma represents a highly aggressive brain tumor with low survival and no response to chemotherapy and radiation therapy. Temozolomide, the current standard of care chemotherapy, improves patient survival by only about 6 months because of several resistance mechanisms, including unmethylated MGMT, which enables repair of chemotherapy-induced DNA damage. Thus, additional treatment strategies are necessary to investigate efficient responses towards glioblastoma.
